subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden NO_REPLY suppression for mixed trailing or own-line payloads, and where should it draw the boundary between silent-intent preamble text and legitimate substantive replies that mention or append the token?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves some substantive trailing-token replies, while this issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; that is a shared message-delivery and security contract choice rather than a mechanical cleanup close.

options.title: Adopt Classifier-Based Suppression
options.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads, preserves legitimate substantive replies, and applies consistently across delivery paths.

options.title: Use Blanket Trailing/Own-Line Suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line NO_REPLY token, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep The Current Narrow Policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-wrapped token-only, JSON, reasoning-prefixed, and scoped cron silent payloads are suppressed, then retarget or close broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt Classifier-Based Suppression
recommendation.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads, preserves legitimate substantive replies, and applies consistently across delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans shared reply delivery, exported matcher behavior, and security/product policy, and steipete has recent central-file and landing history on this surface.
